story: Same average return, very different result: volatility drag

segments.label: MONEY LAB
segments.title: Same average. Far less money.
segments.narration: Two investments average the same five percent a year. One ends with 1.8 times the money of the other.

segments.label: THE SETUP
segments.title: A: +5% every year
segments.narration: Investment A gains five percent every year. Investment B swings: up thirty, then down twenty. Its average is also five percent.

segments.label: 20 YEARS LATER
segments.title: Both start with $10,000
segments.narration: After twenty years, A has about 26,500 dollars. B has about 14,800.

segments.label: THE MATH
segments.title: Losses hurt more than gains help
segments.narration: Losses cut the base that gains grow from. Lose fifty percent, gain fifty, and one hundred dollars becomes 75.

segments.label: THE LESSON
segments.title: B really compounds at 2.0%
segments.narration: So B's real yearly growth is only 2.0 percent. When comparing investments, look at compound growth, not average return.

segments.label: AUGASTER MONEY LAB
segments.title: The math behind money
segments.narration: Education only, not advice. Follow for more Money Lab.
